dedupe_keys.name: asset administration shell aas specifications idta

description: The Asset Administration Shell (AAS) is the Industry 4.0 standard for a digital representation of an industrial asset, linking a physical product or machine with its digital data through standardised submodels. Its specification set covers the metamodel (Part 1, IDTA-01001), application programming interfaces (Part 2), data specifications for IEC 61360 properties and units of measurement (Parts 3a and 3b), security (Part 4) and the AASX package file format (Part 5), with release 26-01 listed at access and earlier versions in an archive. It is maintained by the Industrial Digital Twin Association (IDTA), an international association of industrial technology companies. Coverage is global and cross-industry, with most use in manufacturing and automation. The specifications are listed for download in the IDTA content hub without a price, but the pages read do not state their licence. Caveats: the AAS defines structures, not data, so usefulness depends on which submodel templates suppliers fill in, and the pages read do not describe the tools that implement it. For simulation it provides the standard asset descriptions from which digital twins of plants and equipment can be assembled and exchanged between tools. It is related to the OPC UA and ISA-95 records in this catalogue, which cover communication and enterprise integration in the same plants.
